implementation_notes: Spring's Converter<S,T> is deliberately one-directional, so the two-way pair is formed by registering both converters in a ConversionService (GenericConversionService implements ConverterRegistry) and resolving by (source, target) type; callers inject the ConversionService and never name a converter class, which is what keeps the representations unaware of each other. ConverterFactory and GenericConverter are the escape hatches for whole hierarchies or annotation-driven conversion, and the classic generic Converter<T,U> class holding two java.util.function.Function instances (the catalog's own realization) stays the dependency-free option outside a Spring context.
pitfalls: A ConversionService returns null or throws ConverterNotFoundException when no converter matches; because registration is not checked at compile time, canConvert must guard optional conversions.
Converters are shared singletons and the documentation requires them to be thread-safe and stateless - per-conversion caches keyed on mutable state are a bug.
Only one converter per (source, target) pair survives in the registry; a duplicate registered later silently wins.

variants.name: JPA AttributeConverter<X,Y> for column mapping
variants.implementation_notes: The single-class, both-directions form: AttributeConverter<X,Y> owns convertToDatabaseColumn (attribute to database value) and convertToEntityAttribute (database value to attribute) and is attached with @Convert or autoApply = true, so the entity and the JDBC layer never learn each other's types. It is the persistence-layer equivalent of a converter pair, and the classic generic mapper class is unnecessary while the mapping is one column to one value.
pitfalls: An AttributeConverter must have a public no-argument constructor and cannot be applied to @Id attributes, version columns or relationships.
Providers may pass null on either side, so a converter without null branches fails only on real nullable data.
The converted column still needs its own @Column type or length declaration, otherwise the schema no longer matches what the converter writes.
